top_categories.workout_context: 375 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
375 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 375 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.

Road-specific control matters at Vuelta Puerto Rico. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 375 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Vuelta Puerto Rico's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before February.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what Vuelta Puerto Rico's mixed terrain actually does to you.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Vuelta Puerto Rico's mixed terrain rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
Tempo is Vuelta Puerto Rico's race pace. The wattage you'll hold for 375 miles on mixed terrain. Train it until it's automatic.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Vuelta Puerto Rico. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
At Vuelta Puerto Rico, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Vuelta Puerto Rico. Train it until it feels boring.

race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 375 miles: 80–100g carbs/hour from mile 1 — don’t wait until you’re hungry. Practice your exact race-day nutrition in every long training ride. Carry backup calories. 375 miles burns 8,000–12,000+ calories — you cannot replace them all, but you must try.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Vuelta Puerto Rico rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, HVLI Extended, and Endurance to prepare you for 375 miles of mixed terrain in San Juan (start/finish), full island circumnavigation, Puerto Rico.
